earnings.title: EX-99.1 - 3Q 2026 EARNINGS RELEASE
highlights: For the quarter, the Company reported net income of $476 million, or $2.53 per share.
In the prior year period, the Company reported net income of $586 million, or $2.96 per share.
Closings of 6,876 Homes Generated Home Sale Revenues of $3.9 Billion
Unit Backlog Increased 4% to 10,298 Homes; Backlog Value Increased 3% to $6.4 Billion

quotes.text: With homebuying demand increasingly pressured by rising mortgage rates, widespread inflation, and global unrest, we continue to benefit from our diversified operating platform and consistent strategies for delivering superior returns over the housing cycle.
quotes.by: PulteGroup President and CEO, Ryan Marshall

quotes.text: The rapid increase in interest rates has stretched affordability even further, made selling an existing home even harder, and has pushed even more consumers to the sidelines.

items.heading: Increases in interest rates, reductions in mortgage availability, or other increases in the effective costs of owning a home have prevented potential customers from buying our homes and adversely affected our business and financial results.

The homebuilding industry is cyclical and deteriorations in industry conditions or downward changes in general economic or other business conditions have historically affected our business and financial results and could do so in the future.
Inflation has resulted in increased costs that we may not be able to recoup and has impacted home affordability and consumer sentiment.
Supply shortages and other risks related to the demand for skilled labor and building materials could increase costs and delay deliveries.
Our success depends on our ability to acquire land suitable for residential homebuilding in accordance with our land investment criteria.
If the market value of our land drops significantly, our profits could decrease and result in write-downs of the carrying values of land we own.
